Step 1: Calculate the number of moles of N₂ using the ideal gas law.
$$
n = \frac{PV}{RT}
$$
Where $ P = \frac{36}{22414} $ bar (since 1 cm³ = 1e-6 m³ and 1 bar = 1e-5 m²/s²), $ V = 36 $ cm³ = $ 36 \times 10^{-6} $ m³, $ R = 8.31446261815324 $ J/(mol K), and $ T = 300 $ K.

Step 2: Calculate the number of moles of N₂.
$$
n = \frac{P V}{R T} = \frac{(36 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^3) \times (1 \text{ bar})}{8.31446261815324 \text{ J/(mol K)} \times 300 \text{ K}}
$$
$$
n = \frac{36 \times 10^{-6}}{2494.338785} \approx 1.44 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol}
$$

Step 3: Calculate the change in Gibbs free energy using the formula:
$$
\Delta G = n \cdot R \cdot T \cdot \ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)
$$
Where $ V_1 = 36 $ cm³, $ V_2 = 60 $ cm³, $ R = 8.31446261815324 $ J/(mol K), and $ T = 300 $ K.

Step 4: Calculate the change in Gibbs free energy.
$$
\Delta G = (1.44 \times 10^{-6} \text{ mol}) \cdot (8.31446261815324 \text{ J/(mol K)}) \cdot (300 \text{ K}) \cdot \ln\left(\frac{60}{36}\right)
$$
$$
\Delta G = (1.44 \times 10^{-6}) \cdot (8.31446261815324) \cdot (300) \cdot \ln(1.6667)
$$
$$
\Delta G \approx (1.44 \times 10^{-6}) \cdot (8.31446261815324) \cdot (300) \cdot 0.510825623766
$$
$$
\Delta G \approx 1.44 \times 10^{-6} \cdot 1294.338785 \approx 1.88 \times 10^{-3} \text{ J}
$$

Step 1: Use the formula for the electrostatic force between two point charges: $ F = \frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2} $, where $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $ are the charges, and $ r $ is the distance between them.

Step 2: Plug in the values:
- Charge of an electron: $ q_1 = -1.6 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C} $
- Charge of the dipole: $ q_2 = 3.6 \times 10^{-29} \, \text{C} $
- Distance: $ r = 25 \, \text{nm} = 25 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{m} $

Step 3: Calculate the force:
$$
F = \frac{1}{4\pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}
$$
$$
F = \frac{1}{4\pi \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12}} \frac{(-1.6 \times 10^{-19})(3.6 \times 10^{-29})}{(25 \times 10^{-9})^2}
$$
$$
F = \frac{1}{1.112 \times 10^{-10}} \frac{-5.76 \times 10^{-48}}{625 \times 10^{-18}}
$$
$$
F = \frac{-5.76 \times 10^{-48}}{6.25 \times 10^{-15}} \times \frac{1}{1.112 \times 10^{-10}}
$$
$$
F \approx -8.7 \times 10^{-33} \, \text{N}
$$

Step 1: Use Coulomb's law to find the charge of each ion.
$$
F = k \frac{q^2}{r^2}
$$
Where:
- $ F = 3.7 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{N} $
- $ k = 8.988 \times 10^9 \, \text{N m}^2 / \text{C}^2 $
- $ r = 5.0 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m} $

Step 2: Solve for $ q $.
$$
q^2 = \frac{F \cdot r^2}{k}
$$
$$
q = \sqrt{\frac{F \cdot r^2}{k}}
$$

Step 3: Plug in the values.
$$
q = \sqrt{\frac{(3.7 \times 10^{-9} \, \text{N}) \cdot (5.0 \times 10^{-10} \, \text{m})^2}{8.988 \times 10^9 \, \text{N m}^2 / \text{C}^2}}
$$
$$
q = \sqrt{\frac{(3.7 \times 10^{-9}) \cdot (25 \times 10^{-20})}{8.988 \times 10^9}}
$$
$$
q = \sqrt{\frac{9.25 \times 10^{-28}}{8.988 \times 10^9}}
$$
$$
q = \sqrt{1.03 \times 10^{-37}}
$$
$$
q \approx 3.2 \times 10^{-19} \, \text{C}
$$
